Title: FortiBleed Attack on Fortinet FortiGate Firewalls and SSL VPN Gateways

Victim.Description: Victims are organizations using Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways across 194 countries.

diamond_model_summary: The FortiBleed attack targets Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways using leaked credentials. The adversary employs sophisticated password-cracking techniques and establishes persistence by creating new admin accounts. The attack serves as an entry point for ransomware affiliates, impacting organizations globally.
doc_summary: The FBI warns of ongoing FortiBleed attacks targeting Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways. Hackers use leaked credentials, infostealer logs, credential stuffing, and password spraying to access endpoints. They extract authentication data and crack password hashes offline using a GPU cluster with Hashcat and Hashtopolis. FortiBleed serves as an initial entry point for ransomware affiliates like INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware. Discovered in June, the attack exposed a server with usernames and passwords for 73,932 firewall URLs across 194 countries. SOCRadar linked FortiBleed to credential harvesting operations. Attackers create admin accounts, delete existing ones, and establish persistence. The FBI advises restricting external access, enforcing MFA, and reviewing logs for unauthorized changes.
kill_chain_summary: The FortiBleed attack involves reconnaissance through scanning exposed Fortinet devices, exploitation via credential stuffing, and persistence by creating admin accounts. Attackers use compromised access for ransomware deployment, impacting organizations worldwide. The FBI recommends restricting access and enforcing MFA.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The FortiBleed attack involves credential harvesting and password cracking, making it challenging to detect and remediate. The use of tools like Hashcat and Hashtopolis for offline password cracking highlights the sophistication of the attack. Monitoring for unusual login attempts and auditing admin account changes are crucial for detection.

Title: MALFEX npm Supply Chain Malware Campaign

Victim.Description: Global npm users targeted through supply chain attack.

diamond_model_summary: The MALFEX campaign involves a Portuguese-speaking adversary using npm packages to deliver malware, including Overlord RAT and Node.js stealers. The infrastructure includes Brazilian hosting services for C2, and the victims are global npm users. The campaign is opportunistic, targeting sensitive data through supply chain attacks.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed a long-running npm supply chain malware campaign named MALFEX by CloudSEK and Checkmarx. The campaign involves a lone threat actor who published 12 packages since August 2023, with eight flagged as malicious. The packages have been downloaded 40,767 times, with 'function-flag' being the most downloaded. The campaign uses Overlord RAT loaders and a Node.js stealer to harvest sensitive data. The operator is Portuguese-speaking, with git commits at -0300, and uses npm and Discord for global delivery. Overlord RAT has been seen in other campaigns exploiting WordPress flaws and a macOS campaign with a fake Zoom installer linked to a North Korea-aligned threat cluster.
kill_chain_summary: The MALFEX campaign follows a structured kill chain: reconnaissance to identify npm users, weaponization of npm packages, delivery through npm installations, exploitation via lifecycle hooks, installation of RATs and stealers, command and control through Brazilian hosting services, and actions on objectives by harvesting sensitive data.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the MALFEX campaign includes domain names like cdnzona.discloud.app, tools such as Overlord RAT, and TTPs involving supply chain attacks and remote access trojans. These indicators are crucial for detection and response efforts against the campaign.

Title: Unauthorized HTTPS Certificates Issued for Google Domains via ccTLD Compromise

Victim.Description: Google domains under ccTLDs for Ghana, Sierra Leone, and American Samoa.
Victim.Security_Posture: Compromised due to unauthorized certificate issuance

diamond_model_summary: The incident involved attackers compromising ccTLDs for Ghana, Sierra Leone, and American Samoa to issue unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google domains. The adversary's capability included DNS hijacking and certificate issuance, targeting Google domains. The infrastructure involved compromised ccTLDs and unauthorized certificates. Victims were Google domains under the affected ccTLDs.
doc_summary: In October 2023, attackers compromised three country-code top-level domains (ccTLDs) for Ghana, Sierra Leone, and American Samoa, obtaining unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google domains. The incident involved DNS hijacking, allowing attackers to pose as legitimate Google sites. Google systems were not breached, but domains ending in .gh, .sl, and .as were at risk. Chrome blocked the certificates using CRLSets, and Google worked with certificate authorities to revoke them. Let's Encrypt issued 11 of the 12 certificates, with ZeroSSL issuing one. The certificates were logged between September 22 and 27, 2023. Google advised domain owners to implement strict CAA records to prevent future unauthorized issuance. The incident highlighted vulnerabilities in DNS and certificate issuance processes.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable ccTLDs, followed by weaponization through DNS hijacking. Delivery involved issuing unauthorized certificates for Google domains. Exploitation occurred via DNS record hijacking. Actions on objectives potentially included intercepting encrypted communications. Google responded by blocking certificates and revoking them with CAs.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names such as google.com.gh, google.sl, and google.as, which were used in the unauthorized certificate issuance. The attack leveraged DNS hijacking, a challenging tactic to detect and remediate. The incident highlights the importance of monitoring DNS changes and certificate issuance processes to prevent similar attacks.

Title: Canto Incognito Campaign Targets AI and LLM Infrastructure for Cryptocurrency Mining

Victim.Description: Enterprise deployments of AI and LLM infrastructure targeted for cryptocurrency mining.

diamond_model_summary: The Canto Incognito campaign is attributed to an Italian-speaking threat actor targeting AI and LLM infrastructure for cryptocurrency mining. The adversary uses creative techniques like hiding C2 addresses in poems on GitHub. The infrastructure involves compromised AI systems, and the victims are primarily in the United States and Western Europe. The campaign's objective is to expand a botnet for financial gain.
doc_summary: Canto Incognito is a financially motivated cyber campaign targeting exposed AI and LLM infrastructure to deploy cryptocurrency miners like XMRig and Iron. The campaign uses a creative technique, PoeLLM, to hide C2 addresses within poems hosted on GitHub. The malware has been active since April 2026, affecting over 3400 servers, primarily in the United States and Western Europe. The campaign exploits vulnerabilities in enterprise deployments such as LiteLLM, Gotenberg, Gitea, and Ivanti Sentry appliances. Lumen Black Lotus Labs attributes the activity to an Italian-speaking threat actor, aiming to expand a botnet for cryptocurrency mining. The campaign also involves scanning for similar vulnerable systems and experimenting with distributed brute-force attacks.
kill_chain_summary: The Canto Incognito campaign follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance through scanning for vulnerable AI and LLM systems. Delivery is achieved via HTTP POST requests, followed by exploitation of public-facing applications. Installation involves deploying cryptocurrency miners, with command and control facilitated through GitHub-hosted poems. The final stage involves resource hijacking for cryptocurrency mining.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Canto Incognito campaign presents several indicators across the Pyramid of Pain. Domain names like github.com are used for C2 communication, while tools like XMRig and Iron are employed for cryptocurrency mining. The campaign's TTPs include exploiting AI infrastructure and using GitHub for C2. These indicators provide varying levels of difficulty for defenders to detect and respond to.

Title: Critical Vulnerability in LMCache Allows Remote Code Execution

Victim.Description: Organizations using LMCache in multiprocess mode with routable addresses.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in LMCache, allowing remote code execution via unauthenticated network messages. The flaw is in the multiprocess mode using ZeroMQ, with the potential for exploitation when the server is set to a routable address. JFrog disclosed the vulnerability, which affects versions 0.3.9 to 0.5.5, with no fixed version available. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-105192.
doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in LMCache, an open-source software used to speed up large language model servers like vLLM, allows attackers to execute code on the cache server without authentication. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-105192, affects LMCache versions from 0.3.9 to 0.5.5 and is present in the 0.5.6 release candidates. The vulnerability is in the multiprocess mode where the cache server communicates over the ZeroMQ messaging library. A single network message can execute commands as the user running the LMCache process, which often runs as root. JFrog disclosed the flaw on October 7, 2026, assigning it a critical severity score of 9.8. The vulnerability is exacerbated when the server is set to listen on a routable address. No fixed version is available, and JFrog advises against using a routable address. The flaw involves unpacking messages with Python's pickle format, which can execute code during decoding. A related denial-of-service vulnerability in vLLM, CVE-2026-105756, has been fixed. The core issue is similar to the ShadowMQ flaws found in other AI frameworks.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves exploitation of a public-facing application, specifically the LMCache server in multiprocess mode. The vulnerability allows remote code execution through crafted network messages using ZeroMQ and Python's pickle format. Detection involves monitoring network traffic and unauthorized code execution, while remediation includes restricting server access and avoiding routable addresses.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes tools like ZeroMQ and the pickle format, which are used to exploit the LMCache vulnerability. The TTPs involve exploiting a public-facing application for remote code execution. No specific hashes, IPs, or domains are identified, but the tools and techniques are critical for understanding the attack vector.

Title: CERT-UA Identifies Malicious JavaScript Injection Campaign by UAC-0277

Victim.Description: Users visiting compromised websites, primarily Windows users.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the threat actor UAC-0277, who used malicious JavaScript to inject into over 100 websites, distributing the LunexStealer malware. The adversary's capability includes using the ClickFix technique for MSI package distribution and the EtherHiding technique for domain retrieval. The infrastructure involves compromised websites and smart contracts on the Polygon or Ethereum network. Victims are primarily Windows users visiting these websites, with data types at risk including cookies, browsing history, and credentials.
doc_summary: The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) identified over 100 compromised websites injected with malicious JavaScript to distribute LunexStealer, also known as Psychedelic Stealer. The campaign, observed in September 2026, is attributed to threat cluster UAC-0277. Victims were shown a fake Cloudflare verification page prompting command execution, leading to the download of a malicious MSI package via the ClickFix technique. The EtherHiding technique was used to retrieve domain names and script modes from smart contracts on the Polygon or Ethereum network. Three operating modes were identified, with Mode 2 targeting Windows users from search engine results. LunexStealer installs the LUNARAXE browser extension, masquerading as Microsoft Office Word Editor, to steal cookies, browsing history, and credentials. The NAIVEMESS component provides file system access via a PowerShell-based Native Messaging Host. CERT-UA advises restricting MSI package installations, monitoring msiexec.exe execution, and enabling Microsoft's vulnerable driver blocklist.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable websites for JavaScript injection. Weaponization involves crafting malicious JavaScript, followed by delivery through compromised websites. Exploitation occurs when users execute commands leading to MSI package downloads. Installation involves deploying LunexStealer and the LUNARAXE extension. Command and control are maintained via the NAIVEMESS component communicating with the C2 server. Actions on objectives include stealing cookies, browsing history, and credentials.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes various indicators. Hash values of the MSI packages and browser extensions are critical for detection. Domain names used for fake verification pages and C2 communication are significant. Network host artifacts include the use of PowerShell and Native Messaging Host. Tools like LUNARAXE and NAIVEMESS are employed. TTPs involve JavaScript injection, fake verification pages, and MSI package distribution. These indicators are crucial for detecting and mitigating the threat.

Victim.Description: WordPress sites using vulnerable versions of Ninja Forms and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a threat actor exploiting XSS vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins to gain unauthorized access and control over sites. The attack targets WordPress sites using vulnerable versions of Ninja Forms and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce, with the objective of establishing persistence and control.
doc_summary: Hackers are exploiting stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins Ninja Forms and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce to install backdoors and create rogue admin accounts. The vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-93836 and CVE-2026-94504, affect older versions of these plugins. The campaign was identified by Patchstack researchers, who observed the same JavaScript payload delivered from imgcdn1.com, indicating a single threat actor. The attack involves planting malicious JavaScript in WooCommerce order data or Ninja Forms submissions, which executes when a logged-in administrator loads the content. This allows the attacker to install a malicious plugin masquerading as WP Smart Thumbnails and create a hidden administrator account. Patchstack advises updating to the latest plugin versions to prevent further exploitation.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the delivery of a malicious JavaScript payload via imgcdn1.com, exploiting XSS vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins. Once executed, the payload installs a malicious plugin and creates a rogue admin account, establishing persistence. The adversary uses backdated timestamps and hidden accounts to evade detection, maintaining control over compromised sites.

doc_summary: Google has temporarily stopped accepting product vulnerability reports for its open-source software through its bug bounty program, effective October 1, 2023. This decision affects projects like Go, Angular, and Protocol Buffers. The halt is due to a significant rise in automated submissions, most of which are invalid. Google plans to update the program by the first quarter of 2027. The Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program (OSS VRP) previously offered rewards for vulnerabilities in flagship and important projects, but these have been removed. Supply chain compromises and other security issues like leaked credentials still qualify for rewards. The change was announced on Google's public GitHub and in a post on X. The Go project has also updated its security policy to address reports generated by large language models (LLMs), emphasizing the need for review and filtering.

Title: ClickFix Attack Leveraging Browser Cache Smuggling

Victim.Description: Targets include financial services and governmental organizations, particularly in the United States, France, and Canada.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable to social engineering and cache smuggling

diamond_model_summary: The ClickFix attack involves sophisticated adversaries like Stardust Chollima and Sandworm, leveraging browser cache smuggling to execute VBScript payloads. The infrastructure includes compromised websites and blockchain-based mechanisms for payload delivery. Victims are primarily in the financial and governmental sectors, with a focus on credential theft.
doc_summary: The ClickFix attack described involves browser cache smuggling to execute a malicious VBScript payload. The attack chain includes pre-fetching a script disguised as a PNG file into the browser cache, which is then executed via a command prompt. The VBScript harvests host information using WMI, fetches a PowerShell script from cocojambo.us.com, and downloads a .NET assembly to inject code into a legitimate process. The attack targets browser and device credentials, leveraging compromised websites and fake CAPTCHA lures. Notable threat actors include Stardust Chollima and Sandworm, with motivations linked to espionage and financial gain. The attack exploits vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins and uses blockchain-based infrastructure rotation. Microsoft recommends cloud-delivered protection and monitoring of suspicious browser activity.
kill_chain_summary: The ClickFix attack follows a multi-stage kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable websites, weaponization of payloads disguised as PNG files, and delivery via compromised sites. Exploitation occurs through browser cache execution, followed by installation of VBScript payloads. Command and control is established via HTTP/HTTPS, leading to actions on objectives such as credential harvesting.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The ClickFix attack presents challenges across the Pyramid of Pain, with domain names like cocojambo.us.com and capsysnet.vg being critical indicators. Tools such as PowerShell and VBScript are used for execution, while TTPs include browser cache smuggling and social engineering. The attack's infrastructure and techniques make detection and remediation complex.

Title: Rejetto HFS CVE-2026-61500 Vulnerability Exploitation

Victim.Description: Rejetto HFS deployments in Japan and the United States targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves reconnaissance activity from a China Telecom IP address targeting Rejetto HFS deployments in Japan and the United States. The adversary is exploiting a session-cookie signing weakness in Rejetto HFS, tracked as CVE-2026-61500, which allows for session forgery and remote code execution. The vulnerability was discovered by Horizon3 researchers using Anthropic's Mythos model. The probing activity is likely motivated by the potential for unauthorized access and RCE, with a high impact severity due to the nature of the vulnerability.
doc_summary: Hackers are actively scanning for a Rejetto HFS weak signing key vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-61500, that allows session forgery, account takeover, and remote code execution (RCE). VulnCheck VP of Security Research Caitlin Condon reported that the company's Canary Intelligence honeypots observed probes targeting CVE-2026-61500. The activity appears to be reconnaissance from a single China Telecom IP address probing deployments in Japan and the United States. Rejetto HFS is a file-sharing server tool used for self-hosted file sharing on Windows, Linux, and macOS. CVE-2026-61500 is a session-cookie signing weakness and leakage issue fixed in Rejetto HFS version 3.2.1. Horizon3 researchers discovered the flaw using Anthropic's Mythos model, which identified both the weak signing-key generation and the leak that enabled key recovery. The release of these technical details may have prompted the probing activity targeting CVE-2026-61500. Users of Rejetto HFS are recommended to upgrade to version 3.2.1 or the latest stable release, 3.3.4, as soon as possible.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves reconnaissance activity from a China Telecom IP address, exploiting a session-cookie signing weakness in Rejetto HFS for potential unauthorized access and remote code execution. doc_summary: A critical security flaw, CVE-2026-61500, in Rejetto HTTP File Server (HFS) is actively exploited. The vulnerability, with a CVSS score of 9.3, involves session forgery due to a weak PRNG, allowing attackers to predict keys and gain unauthorized access. Rejetto HFS versions 3.0.0 to 3.2.0 are affected. Exploitation involves reconstructing the PRNG state to forge session cookies, leading to remote code execution. A patch was released in July 2026, but a Python-based PoC exploit was published in late September by Alejandro Ramos. VulnCheck detected exploitation attempts on October 1, 2026, by a Chinese threat actor targeting US hosts. This is the second major vulnerability in Rejetto HFS after CVE-2024-23692.

doc_summary: ShinyHunters, a notorious cyber extortion group, has been linked to multiple high-profile cyber incidents. doc_summary: The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) experienced a data breach affecting up to 200,000 users after hackers accessed its identity and access management system, DTUBasen, using compromised credentials. The breach impacts current and former employees, students, guests, and external partners since 2003. DTU is taking steps to limit the consequences and ensure affected individuals are informed.

Title: Warlock Exploits SharePoint Vulnerabilities in Portuguese and Spanish-speaking Countries

Victim.Description: Organizations in Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries, including critical infrastructure.

diamond_model_summary: The Warlock threat actor, also known as Gold Salem, Longlegs, and Storm-2603, has been exploiting Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities in attacks targeting organizations in Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries. The activity, observed by Symantec and Carbon Black, has impacted critical infrastructure, government, and education sectors. Warlock gained prominence in mid-2025 with the zero-day exploitation of ToolShell SharePoint flaws to deploy ransomware. The group has also been linked to the compromise of SmarterTools by exploiting an unpatched SmarterMail instance. Warlock uses legitimate tools like Velociraptor for command-and-control and the BYOVD technique to disarm security software. The attacks have leveraged multiple vulnerabilities in on-premises SharePoint Server deployments, dropping web shells to collect ASP.NET machine keys for remote code execution. The recent focus on Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries suggests either opportunistic targeting or deliberate tasking.

doc_summary: The UK's domestic intelligence agency, MI5, issued a Security Service Espionage Alert on September 30, 2026, warning that over 100 UK-linked academics have unknowingly contributed to Chinese intelligence efforts. The China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI), also known as the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT), is identified as a front for the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS). CGTRI funds research in AI, cybersecurity, and covert communications, enhancing MSS espionage capabilities. UK academic institutions are urged to review collaborations with CGTRI to avoid prosecution under the National Security Act 2023. The Chinese embassy in the UK denies the allegations, calling them fabricated. A report by the UK-China Transparency think tank highlights forced spying by Chinese students in the UK, further linking CGTRI to MSS through staffing overlaps with China's University of International Relations.

doc_summary: A China-nexus threat actor has launched a campaign targeting government and policy organizations across Asia, including Taiwan, India, and the Philippines. The campaign involves a Rust-compiled Windows backdoor named Antino, which uses Microsoft 365 for command-and-control. Cisco Talos tracks this activity as UAT-11587, which shares similarities with the Jewelbug group. The campaign employs spear-phishing with spoofed sender identities and fake Gmail attachment previews to gain initial access. The attack chain includes HTA or WSF files leading to the deployment of Antino, which supports host reconnaissance, command execution, and persistence. The campaign's focus aligns with China-nexus interests, targeting political and security themes.

Delivery occurs via spear-phishing emails with spoofed sender identities. Exploitation relies on social engineering, leading to the installation of the Antino backdoor via DLL sideloading. Command and control are maintained through Microsoft 365, and actions on objectives include data exfiltration and command execution using PowerShell.

doc_summary: A critical vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-90970 was disclosed by GitLab on October 2, 2023. This flaw affects the AI Gateway, allowing logged-in users with Duo Agent Platform access to execute arbitrary commands under certain conditions. The vulnerability is rated critical with a CVSS score of 9.9. It impacts self-hosted gateways, requiring immediate updates to versions 19.2.4, 19.3.2, or 19.4.1. The flaw involves escaping the prompt template sandbox in custom flows, potentially leading to command execution. GitLab has already patched its hosted gateways, and the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has assessed the exploitation as 'none'. The flaw is similar to a previous issue, CVE-2026-1868, also rated 9.9, involving template engine weaknesses classified under CWE-1336.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves exploiting a critical vulnerability in GitLab's AI Gateway, allowing command execution through a crafted flow configuration. Immediate updates are required to mitigate the risk.

Dell advises customers to update to version 1.18.0 or later to mitigate these risks. diamond_model_summary: The Tren de Aragua group, a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization, executed a sophisticated ATM jackpotting scheme using Ploutus malware. The victims were primarily U.S. financial institutions, resulting in significant financial losses.
doc_summary: The U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned 10 targets involved in a Tren de Aragua ATM jackpotting scheme that stole at least $40.73 million from U.S. financial institutions. The network used cryptocurrency to launder the proceeds. Tren de Aragua is a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization. Jackpotting uses Ploutus malware to force ATMs to dispense cash. Treasury estimates show reported losses totaling $40.73 million from more than 1,500 alleged TdA jackpotting attacks in the United States as of August 2025. TRM Labs said the seven designated crypto wallet addresses have received approximately $6.1 million in total inflows since March 2022. Tren de Aragua is using ATM malware as a terrorist financing tool, then moving the cash onto TRON so it looks like ordinary exchange deposits.
kill_chain_summary: The attack involved multiple stages, starting with the weaponization of Ploutus malware for ATM jackpotting. The delivery and exploitation stages involved deploying the malware to ATMs, followed by installation to maintain persistence. Command and control were achieved through cryptocurrency networks, and the final objective was dispensing cash and laundering it through TRON.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a sophisticated WordPress compromise involving the SC backdoor, which employs blockchain-controlled persistence mechanisms. The malware, described as a self-healing mesh, is capable of reinfecting the site through multiple vectors, including files, databases, and shared memory. The SC backdoor communicates with a command-and-control server using the Ethereum blockchain, allowing threat actors to maintain control over the compromised site. The infection registers cron hooks and can create hidden administrator accounts, inject JavaScript, and deactivate plugins. The attack exploits known vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins and themes, weak credentials, and insecure upload features. The disclosure coincides with the active exploitation of a high-severity SQL injection flaw in the wpForo Forum plugin (CVE-2026-1581).

The adversary can then execute actions on objectives, such as injecting malicious content and maintaining control over the site.

doc_summary: OpenAI identified and disrupted a coordinated distillation campaign by Moonshot AI, a Chinese company, aimed at extracting protected reasoning from AI models. The campaign began on July 1, 2026, and spiked on July 24-25, 2026, with 16,000 requests from over 4,000 users. OpenAI characterized the activity as adversarial distillation, involving unauthorized use of model outputs to train another model. The campaign was fully disrupted on July 28, 2026. Researchers found an architectural vulnerability allowing encrypted reasoning traces to be exploited across sessions and models. This poses safety and national security risks, as extracted reasoning could train models without original safeguards. Moonshot AI has faced similar accusations before, including from Anthropic. The incident highlights the need for robust security measures in AI model development.

doc_summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical pre-authentication command injection vulnerability, CVE-2026-88771, in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway. The LevelBlue THOR team identified malicious authentication events with attacker-controlled usernames to weaponize this vulnerability. The Dutch NCSC issued a warning due to active exploitation. Attackers used variations of 'pitboss' and 'NSPPE' strings, and tools like curl and wget, to drop web shells, steal configuration data, and establish reverse shells. Notable payloads include a Python script for reverse shell to IP 45.141.21.130 and a Perl script with post-exploitation capabilities. Mandiant and Google GTIG reported impacts on dozens of organizations, with PHP web shells like WHIPSHOT and Python tunneler SLAPSHOT being deployed.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain: initial access through exploitation of CVE-2026-88771, delivery of web shells and reverse shell scripts, installation of persistence mechanisms, and command and control via a C2 server. Actions on objectives include data theft and system compromise. Detection and remediation strategies focus on monitoring for unusual activities and applying security patches.

Title: Massive Exposure of Credentials on GitHub Despite Security Measures

Victim.Description: No significant information detected

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the exposure of over 543,000 credentials on GitHub, identified by Truffle Security. Despite GitHub's Push Protection, a significant number of credentials remained exposed, indicating a gap in security measures. The adversary is not identified, but the capability to exploit exposed credentials is evident. The infrastructure involves public GitHub repositories, and the victims are potentially any users whose credentials were exposed.
doc_summary: In 2025, Truffle Security identified over 543,000 unique credentials exposed in public GitHub repositories, despite GitHub's security measures like Push Protection. The analysis covered 224 million repositories and 58 billion files, revealing that credentials remained publicly accessible for a median of 784 days. The study found that 10% of the credentials were older than 6.3 years, with some dating back to 2009. The number of exposed credentials more than doubled compared to previous findings, with secret density increasing from 3.72 per million files in 2015 to 11.62 in 2025. Push Protection, activated for all users in February 2024, reduced exposure in protected categories by 53%, but 51.8% of live credentials were not covered by default protections. The report highlights the need for immediate credential rotation, repository cleanup, and automatic expiration settings to mitigate risks.
kill_chain_summary: The incident primarily involves the exposure of credentials on GitHub, which could be leveraged in various stages of the kill chain. While specific adversary actions are not detailed, the exposure itself represents a significant risk, potentially enabling exploitation and actions on objectives if adversaries access these credentials. The lack of revocation for exposed credentials highlights a vulnerability in the security process.

Other vulnerabilities include path traversal, heap-based buffer overflow, TOCTOU race condition, and improper path validation, which could enable local attackers to execute code remotely or escalate privileges. TeamViewer urged users to update to version 15.82 to address these issues. No evidence of public exploit code or active exploitation was found. TeamViewer has a history of breaches, including incidents involving the Winnti backdoor malware and the Midnight Blizzard group.

doc_summary: AI coding agents inadvertently exposed internal company images by uploading them to public GitHub repositories. doc_summary: Unknown threat actors have been exploiting a newly patched security flaw, CVE-2026-88772, in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances. The attacks, observed by Mandiant Consulting and Google Threat Intelligence Group in September 2026, target sectors including government, financial services, technology, education, and legal services in North America and Europe. The vulnerability allows bypassing authentication and triggers an unhandled termination of the NetScaler Packet Processing Engine, leading to root-level access. The attackers deploy a toolkit with PHP web shells like WHIPSHOT and a Python tunneler SLAPSHOT for internal reconnaissance and credential theft. The flaw is a memory overflow bug in the Datagram Transport Layer Security protocol handling. The attack chain involves modifying httpd.conf files to handle .deb files as PHP scripts, enabling web shell deployment. GreyNoise observed mass exploitation beginning September 28, 2026, with wide-scale web shell and malware deployment for botnet recruitment and access brokering.

Title: Critical Vulnerability Exploitation in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway

Victim.Description: Organizations using Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway, identified as CVE-2026-88772. The vulnerability is a memory overflow bug in the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) protocol handling, which can be exploited for remote code execution or denial-of-service. The adversary exploits the parsing inconsistency in the DTLS handshake header to craft malicious records, leading to buffer overflow. The infrastructure involved includes Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway, with the potential impact being critical due to the possibility of remote code execution with root-level privileges.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed a critical security flaw in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway, tracked as CVE-2026-88772, with a CVSS score of 9.5. This memory overflow bug in the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) protocol handling is rooted in the NetScaler Packet Processing Engine (NSPPE). The vulnerability allows for remote code execution or denial-of-service. The issue arises from NetScaler's implicit trust in the declared fragment size in the DTLS handshake header's fragment_length field, leading to a parsing inconsistency that can be exploited by attackers. The vulnerability has been actively exploited in the wild, with attackers crafting malicious records to cause buffer overflow. The overflow can be weaponized to divert control flow to arbitrary shellcode with root-level privileges. The disclosure follows the release of a proof-of-concept for CVE-2026-88771, which has been abused alongside CVE-2026-88772 in real-world attacks.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves several stages. During the Weaponization stage, adversaries craft malicious DTLS records to exploit the buffer overflow vulnerability. In the Exploitation stage, CVE-2026-88772 is exploited to achieve buffer overflow. The Actions on Objectives stage involves the potential for remote code execution with root-level privileges. The vulnerability allows attackers to divert control flow to arbitrary shellcode, bypassing NX protections. The incident highlights the critical nature of the vulnerability and the need for immediate remediation to prevent exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the exploitation of a specific vulnerability, CVE-2026-88772, which is a significant TTP. The lack of specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names limits the ability to track the adversary's infrastructure. The primary focus is on the TTPs employed, specifically the exploitation of the DTLS protocol handling vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway. The incident underscores the importance of addressing vulnerabilities promptly to mitigate the risk of exploitation.

Title: Malicious Custom GPT Variants Exploit ClickFix Attacks

Victim.Description: Users targeted through sponsored Google results leading to malicious sites.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a threat actor exploiting custom GPT variants hosted on OpenAI's platform to deliver malware via ClickFix attacks. The adversary used legitimate platforms like Google Sites to increase the legitimacy of their operation. The campaign targeted users globally, leveraging social engineering tactics to trick them into executing malicious PowerShell commands. The attack chain included a remote access trojan with capabilities for remote desktop access and data exfiltration.
doc_summary: A malicious campaign exploiting custom variants of OpenAI's ChatGPT was identified by Huntress, targeting users through sponsored Google results. The threat actor used ClickFix attacks to deliver malware, directing users to a fake Cloudflare check on Google Sites, which instructed them to run a PowerShell command. This command installed a remote access trojan (RAT) with capabilities for remote desktop access, audio and camera capture, and more. The campaign involved a custom GPT model named 'Plus 5.6', which was linked to a backup site. The malware achieved persistence by creating a new Run key in the Windows Registry and a scheduled task named 'Canon Configuration Reader'. The attack chain included a custom encrypted file system to conceal the persistence script and RAT. Huntress confirmed at least 40 incidents, with two involving a custom GPT variant. OpenAI took down the first GPT by September 25, but a second GPT was found active on September 27. The campaign later switched to using a Stardock-signed host application.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with reconnaissance to exploit custom GPTs and Google Ads for malware delivery. Weaponization involved creating a custom GPT model to deliver malicious instructions. Delivery was achieved through sponsored Google results leading to malicious sites. Exploitation occurred when users executed a PowerShell command. Installation involved deploying a malicious MSI and a modified DLL. Command and control were established via a RAT, enabling remote access. Actions on objectives included data exfiltration and system control.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like chatgpt.com and google.com, which were used to host malicious content. The adversary employed tools such as PowerShell and a remote access trojan to execute their attack. The use of legitimate platforms and custom GPTs for malware delivery represents a sophisticated tactic, making detection and remediation challenging. The campaign's reliance on social engineering and legitimate infrastructure increases the difficulty of disrupting the attack chain.

doc_summary: Signal, a secure messaging app, released version 8.30, completing the rollout of its secure backups feature across Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, and Windows. This feature allows users to create end-to-end encrypted backups of their chats. The backup system supports Signal-hosted backups and on-device local backups, both encrypted and requiring a recovery key. Hosted backups have an additional key for forward secrecy. Threat actors have shown interest in the recovery key's value. The update brings on-device backups to iOS and desktop, revamps Android backups, and introduces a cross-platform format. Media is stored separately, and duplicate files are minimized. Paying users can purge old media from local storage. Disappearing messages are excluded from backups. The iOS client now supports direct iPhone-to-iPhone transfer using a local encrypted Wi-Fi Aware link. Signal's engineers will focus on improving non-backup systems.

Title: Branch Target Reuse (BTR) Attack on Intel CPUs Running Linux

Victim.Description: Intel CPUs running Linux, specifically targeting JIT engines and the Linux kernel.

diamond_model_summary: The Branch Target Reuse (BTR) attack is a speculative execution vulnerability affecting Intel CPUs running Linux. Researchers at VUsec and Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna demonstrated the attack, which exploits stale branch predictor information to recover root password hashes. The attack highlights the vulnerability of modern CPUs to indirect branch prediction exploits.
doc_summary: A new variant of the Spectre v2 attack, called Branch Target Reuse (BTR), has been discovered by researchers at VUsec and Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna. This attack targets Intel CPUs running Linux, exploiting stale information in the processor's branch predictor. The attack can recover root password hashes by manipulating the CPU into executing incorrect instructions. The vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2026-64507 and CVE-2026-64508, with fixes already merged into the Linux kernel. The attack was tested against Firefox's SpiderMonkey, GraalVM, and the Linux kernel's cBPF, demonstrating the practicality of SMC-based transient execution attacks. The research highlights the inherent vulnerability of modern CPUs to indirect branch prediction exploits.
kill_chain_summary: The BTR attack involves exploiting speculative execution vulnerabilities in Intel CPUs. The attack is weaponized by developing capabilities to exploit these vulnerabilities, leading to the recovery of root password hashes. The exploitation stage involves manipulating the CPU's branch predictor to execute incorrect instructions, allowing attackers to gather sensitive information.

Title: Star Blizzard's Phishing Campaign Targeting Ukraine-Related Entities

Victim.Description: Targets include organizations tied to Ukraine, primarily in the United States and United Kingdom.

diamond_model_summary: The Star Blizzard group, linked to the Russian FSB, has been conducting phishing campaigns targeting entities related to Ukraine. They use fake event invitations to deliver the CosmicPulse backdoor via the RedFlick method. The infrastructure includes compromised email accounts and domains like secure-dns-hub.com. Victims are primarily in the United States and United Kingdom, with a focus on government, NGOs, and think tanks. The group's motivation is espionage, aiming to gather intelligence on Ukraine-related entities.
doc_summary: Russian state hackers known as Star Blizzard have been using fake event invitations to trick people into installing a backdoor on their Windows computers, according to Microsoft. The campaigns, aimed at people and organizations tied to Ukraine, have affected more than 100 organizations since January, mostly in the United States and United Kingdom. Security agencies in the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, and New Zealand said in December 2023 that Star Blizzard almost certainly works under Center 18 of Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB). By 2023, it had already used fake conference and event invitations as bait, often exchanging messages with a target before sending a malicious link. Microsoft counted at least 13 larger campaigns this year, each with tens to hundreds of emails, on top of the group's usual targeted phishing. Since March, those campaigns have used email accounts on WordPress and cPanel websites, which Microsoft is highly confident the group hacked for that purpose. In 2025, the group delivered its malware through fake CAPTCHA pages that tricked targets into running commands themselves, a method known as ClickFix. This year it switched to a method Microsoft calls RedFlick. RedFlick uses scheduled tasks, jobs that Windows runs automatically, to install a backdoor named CosmicPulse. The invitations name well-known think tanks or NGOs as hosts, such as Chatham House and the Atlantic Council. Many emails are written to appear to come from within the target's organization. The first email usually carries no attachment. If the target replies, the group sends a password-protected RAR or ZIP archive, with the password shown in an image. Microsoft traced several versions of the infection chain. In all of them, a shortcut (LNK) file disguised as a PDF initiates the attack, and a Windows Installer (MSI) package sets up scheduled tasks. The next stage is a downloader disguised as a Control Panel item. It installs CosmicPulse, a Python-based backdoor.
kill_chain_summary: Star Blizzard's attack begins with reconnaissance to identify Ukraine-related targets. They weaponize phishing emails with malicious links, delivering them to targets. Exploitation occurs when users interact with these emails, leading to the installation of the CosmicPulse backdoor via the RedFlick method. Command and control is established through communication with the C2 server at secure-dns-hub.com. The final stage involves exfiltration of sensitive data and credentials. Detection and remediation efforts focus on monitoring email traffic, network activity, and scheduled tasks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses like 103.160.59.97 and domains such as secure-dns-hub.com, which are critical for detection and blocking. The use of tools like RedFlick and malware like CosmicPulse are significant indicators of compromise. Network host artifacts, such as unusual scheduled tasks, provide additional detection opportunities. The TTPs employed by Star Blizzard, including phishing and backdoor installation, are crucial for understanding their attack methods and improving defenses.

Title: Branch Target Reuse (BTR) Spectre Variant Exploits JIT Engines

Victim.Description: JIT engines in web browsers, language runtimes, and operating system kernels.

diamond_model_summary: The Branch Target Reuse (BTR) variant of the Spectre vulnerability targets JIT engines in web browsers and operating system kernels. It exploits stale indirect branch prediction entries to hijack transient control flow, allowing attackers to bypass software hardening and leak sensitive data. The vulnerability affects multiple CPU vendors and has been demonstrated against SpiderMonkey, GraalVM, and the Linux kernel. Mitigations have been released for the Linux kernel, and other platforms are considering various defenses.
doc_summary: A new Spectre CPU vulnerability variant, Branch Target Reuse (BTR), has been disclosed by researchers from VUSec and Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna. This variant affects Just-In-Time (JIT) engines in web browsers, language runtimes, and operating system kernels across multiple CPU vendors. BTR exploits stale indirect branch prediction entries in JIT engines, allowing attackers to hijack transient control flow and bypass software hardening. The vulnerability impacts SpiderMonkey, GraalVM, and the Linux kernel's cBPF JIT. Proof-of-concept exploits demonstrate the ability to leak root password hashes from fully patched Intel systems. Mitigations have been released for the Linux kernel under CVE-2026-64507 and CVE-2026-64508. The disclosure follows a similar speculative execution attack technique called Interrupt Injection by MIT CSAIL researchers.
kill_chain_summary: The BTR variant of Spectre involves exploiting stale indirect branch prediction entries in JIT engines, allowing attackers to hijack transient control flow and leak sensitive data. The attack requires the ability to run unprivileged code in a JIT engine and targets speculative execution vulnerabilities. Mitigations have been released for the Linux kernel, and other platforms are considering defenses such as randomizing JIT code-cache locations and deploying site isolation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The BTR variant of Spectre does not provide specific indicators such as hashes, IPs, or domains, making it challenging to detect using traditional methods. The attack exploits speculative execution vulnerabilities in JIT engines, requiring mitigations at the software and hardware levels. The lack of specific indicators highlights the difficulty in detecting and responding to such attacks, emphasizing the need for comprehensive defenses against speculative execution vulnerabilities.

Title: PhantomSub Campaign: Malicious npm Packages Exploiting WhatsApp

Victim.Description: Developers using npm packages for WhatsApp integration.

diamond_model_summary: The PhantomSub campaign involves adversaries exploiting npm packages to add developers to WhatsApp groups without consent. The adversary's capability includes modifying npm packages to exploit the Baileys project. The infrastructure involves npm repositories and WhatsApp groups, targeting developers globally. The victim profile includes developers using npm packages for WhatsApp integration, with a medium impact severity.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a cluster of 101 npm packages used in a WhatsApp group subscription campaign called PhantomSub. These packages exploit the Baileys WhatsApp open source project to add victims to groups without consent. The packages have been downloaded 490,000 times, with 116,000 downloads in the last 30 days. The activity was first detected in August 2026 by SafeDep, which found Baileys npm forks engaging in malicious behaviors. OX Security identified three malware variants, with one group based in Indonesia advertising mobile games and applications. Developers are advised to check for unauthorized group additions, block them, and avoid using packages requiring WhatsApp account connections.

Delivery occurs through npm repositories, leading to exploitation of the Baileys project. Installation happens via npm package installation, followed by command and control through WhatsApp groups. The final stage, actions on objectives, involves unauthorized group subscriptions for financial gain.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the PhantomSub campaign includes tools like Baileys and TTPs such as unauthorized group subscription and advertising injection. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names were identified. The campaign's reliance on npm packages and WhatsApp groups highlights the importance of monitoring package installations and group memberships to detect and mitigate such threats.

doc_summary: RatHat's operators have developed an Android banking trojan that is controlled via a web console, as reported by Cleafy. The malware operates under a malware-as-a-service model, with nearly 100 console deployments since April 2026. The console collects data from infected phones, including text messages and passwords, and uses Google's Gemini AI model to estimate victims' bank balances. The malware has remained largely unchanged since late 2025, but the console has been updated multiple times, with versions named BlackCat Remote Control Management and Panda Workshop V5 and V6. The malware is distributed through text messages and online ads, requesting Accessibility access to enable wireless debugging and connect to the Android Debug Bridge. The Go program used by the malware allows for screen capture without user permission. The malware persists even after app removal, and Cleafy identified several indicators for the consoles' command-and-control servers and download links. The infrastructure includes IP addresses primarily from a Singapore-registered network, AS4907.

doc_summary: AI agents authenticate and act across enterprise systems with delegated authority, governed by IAM for AI Agents. This identity-control architecture faces challenges due to identity dark matter, where agents, credentials, and authentication paths are not reported by central identity data. Conventional IAM platforms express intended access, but applications reveal actual execution, creating an intent-to-execution gap. AI agents, unlike human users, dynamically chain tasks and select tools, leading to excessive agency as described in OWASP's Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications (LLM06). Static role assignments and configuration reviews cannot bound agent behavior, and misconfiguration does not automatically lead to exploitability. Agent identities are often created by infrastructure automation, bypassing governance workflows and accumulating outside compliance reporting inventories. An effective agent identity framework must establish distinct identities, constrain actions, and prove execution. Credential design should favor workload identity federation and short-lived credentials. OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange provides delegation semantics, preserving the distinction between agent identity and authority. Continuous monitoring and behavioral analysis are crucial for detecting identity attacks, as legitimate credentials can generate normal-looking authentication records. Orchid Security discovers agent identities directly from applications and infrastructure, complementing enterprise IAM platforms by adding verification and remediation layers.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed a new botnet malware called Carbonato targeting exposed Docker daemons to deploy the Hermes Agent AI framework. The botnet exploits unauthenticated Docker daemons on port 2375, propagating through networks and using Telegram for command and control. The operation was discovered via a public Docker registry accessible since May 2026. Carbonato possesses worm-like capabilities, spreading to other hosts and establishing persistence through cron jobs and watchdog scripts. The Hermes Agent framework is used to execute tasks, collect credentials, and maintain persistence. The attack infrastructure includes a reverse SSH tunnel to Costa Rica and masquerades as a system component to evade detection. The activity has not been attributed to any known threat actor, but clues suggest operators are based in Costa Rica. The incident highlights the growing use of AI tools in cyber attacks, with significant implications for cybersecurity resilience.
kill_chain_summary: The Carbonato botnet follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance through scanning for exposed Docker daemons. diamond_model_summary: The JADEPUFFER attack on Microsoft Azure demonstrates a sophisticated use of AI and known vulnerabilities to execute a ransomware operation. doc_summary: The threat actor JADEPUFFER orchestrated a ransomware attack within a Microsoft Azure environment, leveraging compromised service principals. Microsoft tracked this activity as Storm-3168, noting it as an evolution in the threat actor's tradecraft. The attack occurred in June 2026, targeting Azure Storage Accounts, SQL databases, Key Vaults, and more. JADEPUFFER exploited a security flaw in Langflow (CVE-2025-3248) to gain access, using MySQL's AES_ENCRYPT() for encryption and deploying a Go-based ransomware strain, ENCFORGE, aimed at AI infrastructure. The attack involved reconnaissance, lateral movement, and destructive operations, with over 100 storage account deletion attempts. Microsoft observed compromised service principals linked to the same tenant, used for reconnaissance and destructive operations. The attack highlights a shift towards AI-orchestrated attacks, with the end goal assessed as ransomware-aligned.
kill_chain_summary: JADEPUFFER's attack followed a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance using compromised service principals, followed by exploitation of a known vulnerability in Langflow. The adversary then conducted destructive operations, targeting Azure resources and attempting to delete storage accounts. The attack underscores the need for robust security measures and monitoring in cloud environments.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The JADEPUFFER attack involved several indicators of compromise, including the use of a known vulnerability (CVE-2025-3248) and the ENCFORGE ransomware. Title: Reactivation of Compromised GitHub Actions in Mini Shai-Hulud Campaign

Victim.Description: Developers using compromised GitHub Actions in their workflows.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to reliance on third-party actions.

diamond_model_summary: The Mini Shai-Hulud campaign involved the reactivation of compromised GitHub Actions, targeting developers' credentials and CI/CD secrets. The adversary leveraged supply chain vulnerabilities to distribute malware through GitHub repositories. The incident highlights the risks associated with third-party dependencies in software development environments.
doc_summary: In September 2026, two GitHub Actions, actions-cool/issues-helper and actions-cool/maintain-one-comment, were re-enabled after being compromised in a Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. The actions, previously disabled by GitHub for pointing to malicious code, were accessible again from September 16 to September 25, 2026. This reactivation allowed workflows referencing these actions to download and execute malware targeting developers' tokens, credentials, and CI/CD secrets. The incident affected repositories on the Node Package Manager (npm) index. GitHub's dependency graph lists about 15,000 repositories depending on 'issues-helper', though not all were compromised. Socket researchers identified the issue and recommended removing references to the actions or pinning a verified clean commit. The actions were disabled again on September 25, 2026.
kill_chain_summary: The attack involved the delivery of malicious code via compromised GitHub Actions, leading to the execution of obfuscated payloads targeting developer credentials. The adversary's objective was to collect sensitive information, such as tokens and CI/CD secrets, from affected workflows. The incident underscores the importance of securing third-party dependencies and monitoring for unauthorized changes.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of compromised GitHub Actions as tools for delivering malware. The adversary employed obfuscation techniques to evade detection. doc_summary: A high-severity CSRF vulnerability was discovered in the Elementor Website Builder WordPress plugin, affecting versions 4.3.0 and 4.3.1. Victim.Description: WordPress sites using Elementor plugin versions 4.3.0 and 4.3.1.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a CSRF vulnerability in the Elementor plugin for WordPress, allowing adversaries to create unauthorized admin accounts. The adversary exploits the vulnerability by tricking logged-in administrators into clicking malicious links, leading to unauthorized REST API actions. The infrastructure involves delivering these links via email, chat, or comments. The victims are WordPress sites using Elementor versions 4.3.0 and 4.3.1, with the impact being unauthorized access and control over the sites.
doc_summary: A cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in the Elementor plugin for WordPress allows unauthenticated attackers to create administrator accounts. The flaw affects versions 4.3.0 and 4.3.1 and is exploited by tricking a logged-in administrator into opening a malicious link. This causes the victim's session to perform a REST API action, resulting in the creation of an attacker-controlled admin account. The vulnerability was reported by security firm Patchstack on September 22, 2023, after being discovered by bug hunter Saggre. Elementor released a fix in version 4.3.2. The flaw is due to the Editor Events module bypassing WordPress's REST nonce validation. The attack can be executed without JavaScript or a form, and the malicious link can be delivered via email, chat, or site comments. Users are advised to upgrade to version 4.3.2 to mitigate the risk.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the delivery of malicious links to logged-in administrators, exploiting a CSRF vulnerability in the Elementor plugin. Once the link is clicked, the adversary can execute unauthorized REST API actions, leading to the creation of an attacker-controlled admin account. The exploitation stage involves bypassing WordPress's REST nonce validation, and the installation stage results in unauthorized admin account creation. The attack concludes with the adversary gaining control over the WordPress site.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the exploitation of a CSRF vulnerability in the Elementor plugin, which is a significant TTP. The attack does not involve specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names, focusing instead on exploiting a software vulnerability. Title: Reactivation of Compromised GitHub Actions in Mini Shai-Hulud Campaign

Victim.Description: Victims include developers and organizations using the compromised GitHub Actions in their CI/CD pipelines.
Victim.Security_Posture: Compromised due to reliance on mutable tags.

diamond_model_summary: The Mini Shai-Hulud campaign involved the compromise of GitHub Actions to harvest credentials from CI/CD pipelines. The adversary leveraged existing infrastructure, including the domain t.m-kosche.com, to exfiltrate data. Victims were primarily in the software development sector, with high exposure potential due to the widespread use of GitHub Actions. The incident underscores the importance of securing software supply chains and implementing SHA pinning to prevent similar attacks.
doc_summary: In September 2026, two GitHub Actions were re-enabled after being compromised in the May 2026 Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. The actions, used for issue and comment housekeeping, were exploited to run malicious code that harvested sensitive credentials from CI/CD pipelines. The exfiltration domain t.m-kosche.com linked the activity to the Mini Shai-Hulud cluster, also associated with npm packages from the @antv ecosystem. Despite being disabled, the repositories became accessible again, allowing the malicious payload to execute without new exploits. The incident highlights the risks of mutable tags in software supply chains and the importance of SHA pinning to prevent dependency on upstream repository states.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with the exploitation of compromised GitHub Actions, allowing the adversary to execute malicious code within CI/CD pipelines. This led to the collection of sensitive credentials, which were exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled domain. The incident highlights the risks associated with mutable tags in software supply chains and the need for robust detection and remediation strategies to prevent unauthorized access and data exfiltration.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the domain t.m-kosche.com, which was used for data exfiltration. The use of legitimate GitHub Actions as a tool for malicious purposes presents a challenge for detection and remediation. The incident emphasizes the importance of monitoring for unusual activity in CI/CD pipelines and implementing SHA pinning to mitigate the risk of supply chain compromises.

Title: PamStealer Variant with Server-Side Decryption Chain

Victim.Description: The victims are macOS users targeted through phishing websites and malicious downloads.

diamond_model_summary: The PamStealer incident involves a sophisticated adversary using server-side decryption and dynamic key exchange to protect its payload. The infrastructure includes a fake website (wavel.app) and server-side components. The victims are macOS users targeted through phishing websites. The malware employs advanced techniques such as JXA droppers and Swift-based stealers.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a new version of PamStealer that uses a server-side decryption chain to protect its payload. The malware employs a JavaScript for Automation (JXA) dropper mechanism, with changes in the lure and delivery method. The decoy involves a fake website advertising a non-existent cryptocurrency wallet service named Wavel. The payload is encrypted and requires a server-side key exchange for decryption, making static analysis difficult. The malware also uses Git hooks for persistence and targets macOS systems, including less common browsers like Arc and Zen. The stealer component is now written in Swift, marking a shift from Rust in previous versions.
kill_chain_summary: The PamStealer attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify targets and develop phishing lures. The weaponization stage involves creating a JXA dropper and a Swift-based stealer. Delivery is achieved through a fake cryptocurrency website. The malware installs persistence mechanisms using Git hooks and relies on server-side decryption for command and control. The final objective is to steal sensitive information from macOS users.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the PamStealer incident includes domain names like wavel.app and tools such as JXA droppers and Swift-based stealers. The use of server-side decryption and dynamic key exchange makes it challenging to detect and analyze the malware statically. The adversary's reliance on server-side components for payload decryption adds complexity to the detection and response efforts.

The adversary exploited vulnerabilities in the backend wallet-service system to conduct unauthorized transfers of $351.6 million. doc_summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Bitget disclosed a security breach involving the theft of $351.6 million from its hot and warm wallets, attributed to suspected North Korean hackers. The breach was discovered after unauthorized transfers were flagged by security systems. Bitget has suspended withdrawals and is investigating with law enforcement, Mandiant, and SlowMist. The attack affected multiple blockchain assets, including ETH, XRP, BNB, AVAX, USDT, and USDC. The User Protection Fund, holding 5,500 BTC, will cover the losses. The attack method aligns with known North Korean patterns, and some hacker wallet addresses have been frozen. The incident highlights the ongoing threat of state-backed cybercrime targeting cryptocurrency exchanges.

The adversary exploited these vulnerabilities to gain initial access and conducted unauthorized transfers of cryptocurrency assets. The attack method is consistent with known North Korean patterns, and some hacker wallet addresses have been frozen. The incident highlights the need for robust security measures in cryptocurrency exchanges.

Title: Rydox Marketplace Shutdown and Arrest of Administrators

Victim.Description: Thousands of U.S. citizens had their personal information sold on Rydox.

diamond_model_summary: The Rydox marketplace incident involves Ardit Kutleshi and associates operating an illegal online platform for selling stolen data and cybercrime tools. The infrastructure included servers in Kuala Lumpur and the domain rydox.cc. Victims were primarily U.S. citizens whose personal information was sold. The operation was financially motivated, with cryptocurrency used for transactions.
doc_summary: A Kosovar national, Ardit Kutleshi, pleaded guilty to operating Rydox, an illegal online marketplace selling stolen personal information, login credentials, credit card details, and cybercrime tools. The arrests of Kutleshi and two other administrators, Jetmir Kutleshi and Shpend Sokoli, were part of a joint international law enforcement operation involving Kosovo, Albania, and the Royal Malaysian Police. The operation led to the seizure of the Rydox domain and its servers in Kuala Lumpur. Ardit Kutleshi was extradited to the United States in 2025 and charged with conspiracy to commit identity theft, aggravated identity theft, access device fraud, and money laundering. Rydox facilitated over 7,600 sales of stolen data and offered over 321,000 cybercrime products to more than 18,000 users. Cryptocurrency was used for transactions, and the marketplace charged a fee for authorized sellers. Kutleshi faces up to 20 years in prison for money laundering and a minimum of two years for aggravated identity theft.
kill_chain_summary: The Rydox marketplace facilitated the sale of stolen data and cybercrime tools, with actions on objectives including the collection and sale of sensitive information. The marketplace used application layer protocols for communication and required cryptocurrency for transactions. The operation was disrupted by international law enforcement, leading to the arrest and extradition of key operators.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Rydox incident highlights the use of domain names and tools as key indicators. The domain rydox.cc was central to operations, and cryptocurrency wallets were used for transactions. These indicators are crucial for detection and disruption efforts. The seizure of the domain and servers was a significant step in dismantling the marketplace.

Title: Active Exploitation of Roundcube Webmail SQL Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-48842

Victim.Description: Organizations using vulnerable versions of Roundcube Webmail.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a suspected China-aligned adversary exploiting a SQL injection vulnerability in Roundcube Webmail. The adversary, identified as UNK_MassTraction, targets exposed Roundcube instances to harvest sensitive email communications. The capability involves exploiting CVE-2026-48842, a pre-authentication SQL injection flaw. The infrastructure includes over 523,000 exposed Roundcube instances, with 10 flagged as vulnerable. Victims are organizations using vulnerable Roundcube versions, with potential data exposure including email credentials and stored messages.
doc_summary: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security has issued a warning about the active exploitation of a now-patched vulnerability in Roundcube Webmail, identified as CVE-2026-48842. This vulnerability, with a CVSS score of 8.1, is a pre-authentication SQL injection flaw in the virtuser_query plugin affecting Roundcube Webmail versions 1.6.x before 1.6.16 and 1.7.x before 1.7.1. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary SQL statements, potentially exposing mail account credentials and stored messages. SentinelOne highlighted the risk of SQL injection into Roundcube's database backend. Patches were released in May 2026, but the vulnerability is still being exploited in the wild, as reported by the Cyber Centre. Shadowserver Foundation data indicates over 523,000 Roundcube instances are exposed to the internet, with 10 flagged as vulnerable. Proofpoint identified a China-aligned adversary, UNK_MassTraction, exploiting Roundcube vulnerabilities to deliver web shells or the VShell tool. Previous vulnerabilities in Roundcube, such as CVE-2025-49113 and CVE-2025-68461, were also actively exploited.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with the exploitation of a SQL injection vulnerability in Roundcube Webmail (CVE-2026-48842). The adversary gains initial access through this vulnerability, potentially leading to credential harvesting and data exfiltration. The exploitation stage is critical, with the adversary leveraging the vulnerability to inject arbitrary SQL statements. Actions on objectives may include data collection and credential dumping, with the adversary's ultimate goal being the theft of sensitive email communications.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes TTPs such as SQL injection and web shell deployment, which are challenging for defenders to address. The lack of specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names in the available data limits the ability to apply more straightforward detection and blocking measures. The focus should be on detecting and mitigating the exploitation of the SQL injection vulnerability and monitoring for unusual database activities. The scoring reflects the emphasis on TTPs, which are more difficult to change and require strategic defensive measures.

doc_summary: A vulnerability in Cloudflare Containers allowed customers to access residual data from other customers' containers due to improper disk wiping. The flaw was reported by Oren Yomtov from Accomplish on September 4, 2023, and involved shared disk space using thin provisioning. Cloudflare fixed the issue by re-enabling disk wiping and retiring affected container disks. The incident affected Cloudflare Containers and Sandboxes, but not Browser Run. No evidence of exploitation beyond authorized testing was found. The flaw was disclosed on September 19, 2023.
kill_chain_summary: The vulnerability in Cloudflare Containers allowed unauthorized access to residual data due to improper disk wiping. The flaw was exploited by writing small blocks to disk and reading back the entire block, revealing data from previous containers. Cloudflare fixed the issue by re-enabling disk wiping and retiring affected container disks.

diamond_model_summary: The MacSync malware campaign demonstrates a sophisticated adversary using social engineering and public iCloud calendar events to deliver payloads. The adversary's capability includes a Swift-based info-stealer with evolving modules and an Objective-C backdoor disguised as Finder. The infrastructure leverages iCloud for command delivery, and the victims are macOS users targeted through fake applications and social media promotions.
doc_summary: A new variant of the MacSync info-stealing malware targets macOS systems using public iCloud calendar events to deliver payloads. MacSync, a Swift-based malware, emerged in April 2025 and is delivered disguised as Homebrew and macOS disk space analyzer tools. Kaspersky researchers note that MacSync evolved from the AMOS stealer family, adding new capabilities via modules. It is distributed through social engineering, including ClickFix-style attacks, and software presented as free or cracked. The malware was also delivered as a fake crypto wallet called Toria, promoted on social media. The campaign uses a downloader to fetch commands hidden in iCloud calendar events, downloading the next-stage payload. The infostealer module targets browser history, cookies, saved credentials, crypto wallet data, Telegram data, Keychain files, system information, SSH, AWS, Kubernetes, Git, and shell configuration files. An Objective-C backdoor disguises itself as Finder, establishing persistence through LaunchAgent, .zshrc modifications, and global Git hooks, while terminating macOS notification processes. Kaspersky identified a mystery command downloading an unknown component. MacSync's evolution and distribution chains pose a threat to macOS users, who are advised to avoid executing online commands and downloading suspicious DMG files.
kill_chain_summary: The MacSync campaign follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify targets and weaponization by developing a Swift-based malware with new capabilities. Delivery is achieved through social engineering and disguised applications, while installation involves a dropper establishing persistence. Command and control are maintained via iCloud calendar events, and actions on objectives focus on stealing sensitive information from macOS systems.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The MacSync campaign presents challenges in detection and response due to its use of public iCloud calendar events for command delivery and a backdoor disguised as Finder. The pyramid of pain is populated with TTPs related to social engineering and malware delivery methods, but lacks specific indicators like hashes or IP addresses. This makes traditional detection methods less effective, emphasizing the need for behavioral analysis and user education.

Title: Carbonato Botnet Targets Docker Daemons with Hermes Agent AI

Victim.Description: Victims are Docker hosts with exposed APIs, potentially across various industries.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to lack of authentication on Docker APIs.

diamond_model_summary: The Carbonato botnet targets Docker hosts with exposed APIs, using the Hermes Agent AI framework for control. The adversary, potentially based in Costa Rica, employs advanced techniques such as reverse SSH tunnels and Telegram for C2 communication. Victims are Docker hosts, with high impact severity due to the malware's persistence and data collection capabilities.
doc_summary: The Carbonato botnet malware targets insecure Docker hosts, exploiting exposed APIs on port 2375 to install the Hermes Agent AI framework. Discovered by Malwarebytes, the malware features worm-like capabilities, spreading across Docker hosts without authentication. It launches privileged containers, opens reverse SSH tunnels, and reports deployments via Telegram. Persistence is achieved through cron jobs, systemd timers, and other mechanisms. The AI agent, Hermes, handles task commands, collecting sensitive data and executing commands. The attack spans from October 2024 to August 2026, with Costa Rica as a possible operator location. Indicators include GH0ST persona files, unexpected Telegram traffic, and reverse SSH tunnels.
kill_chain_summary: The Carbonato botnet follows a structured attack pattern, starting with reconnaissance to identify exposed Docker APIs. It exploits these APIs to deliver and install the Hermes Agent AI framework, achieving persistence through cron jobs and systemd timers. Command and control is maintained via Telegram, allowing the adversary to execute commands and collect sensitive data.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Carbonato botnet's indicators include the use of specific tools like Hermes Agent AI and GH0ST, as well as communication protocols such as SSH and Telegram. These indicators are challenging to change, making them valuable for detection and response efforts. The malware's persistence mechanisms and C2 communication channels are key points for monitoring and mitigation.
